rows.description:
This short educational video explains key YouTube Shorts performance metrics, focusing on hooks and viewer retention.
Main points covered:

The shorter a Short is, the higher its retention rate needs to be for YouTube to push it.
“Stated to watch” (or start-to-watch) percentage shows whether your opening hook successfully convinced people to keep watching.
A low start-to-watch rate usually means either:
The opening didn’t immediately show value, or
YouTube tested the video with the wrong audience.

Every video you upload teaches both you and the algorithm more about what your audience likes.
Consistently posting quality content builds a pool of returning viewers, which helps future videos perform better from the start.

rows.title: Second Hook Retention: The Sentence That Decides If Viewers Stay
rows.description:
Second hook retention: hook one gets the click, hook two keeps the watch.
Hook two is the sentence at seconds four to six, and it is where most videos leak viewers.

Saying "here's why" at second four is a dead giveaway that you are stalling.
State the counterintuitive claim instead, then check seconds four to six on your last few videos.
